subject: Clarifying multi-region failover commitments for enterprise contract
messages:
From: Nate Coleman <nate@clearbridge-payments.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying failover guarantees for enterprise contract

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we draft the commercial agreement we need to be explicit about multi-region failover commitments for our payments workload. Two specific asks from our ops/security team: 1) target RTO for region-to-region failover (we are looking for 30 minutes or less for critical payment flows), and 2) RPO expectations (tolerable data loss window).

Also need confirmation on whether Redwood can support a hot-standby standby region with pre-provisioned capacity and the audit logs we’ll need for our compliance review. If you cannot meet the 30-minute RTO without a pricing add-on, please outline the options and the operational tradeoffs.

I attached our internal runbook and failure scenarios for context. Can we get a written summary of the options by EOD Thursday so our procurement team can incorporate it into the SOW?

—Nate
Nate Coleman
Head of Platform Reliability
ClearBridge Payments
[Attachment: cbpay-runbook-excerpts.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Coleman <nate@clearbridge-payments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying failover guarantees for enterprise contract

Hi Nate — thanks for the clear asks and the runbook. High level answers up front, then specifics below:

- Standard hosted SLA: 99.95% regional availability; we do not offer an explicit multi-region RTO commitment on our hosted tier.
- For sub-30-minute RTO we require a Dedicated or Private deployment with pre-provisioned capacity (hot-standby) and a runbook-driven warm cache strategy. That can be contractually committed as an SLA amendment for enterprise deals.
- Typical RPO we can guarantee with continuous replication: up to 60 seconds for request/append logs; longer windows if you depend on client-side buffering.

Options we propose (attached as a short options deck):
1) Hot-standby (Recommended) — Dedicated standby cluster in a second region, pre-warmed, health probes routed by smart routing layer. Estimated RTO: 15–30 minutes for critical flows. Additional monthly commitment: +30% on your base Dedicated capacity.
2) Warm-standby — capacity reserved but not fully warmed; RTO: 2–4 hours. Lower cost uplift.
3) Failover with progressive fallback — no guaranteed RTO; automatic fallback to compatible model variants, best-effort.

Operational notes: warming KV caches and model context is the main driver of the RTO; we’ll need a short list of critical endpoints and a test plan to validate failover windows.

Next steps: Marcus and Laura are looping in technical sizing and the legal language. Would you be available for a 45-minute call Thursday 10:00–11:00 PT to agree on the pilot scope? If so we’ll follow up with a draft SLA amendment and pricing.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-multi-region-options.pdf (PDF)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Nate Coleman <nate@clearbridge-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 07:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying failover guarantees for enterprise contract

Nate, Vanessa — adding technical detail from the infra side.

Quick summary: delivering a 30-minute RTO for payment-critical endpoints is achievable but requires three things: 1) hot-standby cluster with pre-provisioned GPU capacity, 2) automated routing and DNS/traffic cutover with health checks, and 3) KV-cache replay/warmth strategy. In practice the most time-consuming step is restoring any large KV caches and session state for in-flight flows.

We propose the following concrete commitments for the SLA amendment (draft to follow):
- Failover initiation window: ≤ 5 minutes from detection to cutover initiation (monitoring + operator trigger or automated playbook).
- Target measurable RTO: 15–30 minutes for 95% of failover events for endpoints listed in appendix A (we’ll capture these in the SOW).
- RPO: ≤ 60 seconds for tokenized transaction logs; for non-tokenized payloads we can provide per-endpoint RPO in the SOW.
- Auditability: full event timeline and routing decisions logged to your audit export for 180 days.

Sizing estimate: for your peak QPS (per our demo) we recommend reserving 1.5x baseline capacity in standby to avoid degraded latency during cutover. I attached a quick sizing worksheet.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hot-standby-sizing.xlsx (XLSX)]

Vanessa/Marcus — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two follow-ups: 1) procurement wants a sample SLA amendment we can hand to their counsel, and 2) security wants confirmation that the audit export will include the full pre- and post-cutover request/response IDs (redacted as needed) for forensic timelines.

We’re prepared to agree to the hot-standby option with the 15–30 minute RTO if you can provide the amendment and DocuSign-ready SOW. Can we run a two-week pilot where we exercise a failover in a non-production window and measure the actual RTO? If that pilot meets the SLA, we’ll sign the amendment and move forward.

On the pilot: availability Thursday or Friday next week for the dry run.

—Nate
